description: Price-PREFERENCE slice. Isolates the composite score's `economic` weight, which the main 60-query set cannot observe: every economic query there carries a hard threshold (max_price/min_price), so all in-budget hotels tie at grade 2 and a profile with economic=0.000 scores identically to one with 0.200. These queries use graded ladders (evaluation/gold.py _v_ladder_lower) so that returning the CHEAPEST qualifying hotels first scores higher than returning merely-affordable ones. Cut points are absolute LKR, frozen here rather than derived from the live pool, so the gold is not a restatement of the retriever's own pool-percentile economic score. Tiers were set from the Colombo pool (34 of 58 hotels priced; p25 22,226, median 34,126, p75 44,448): cheaper -> 10 hotels at grade 2, 14 at grade 1, 10 at grade 0. NOTE: no query here combines price with a specific amenity, because the pool is bimodal by source - the 34 LiteAPI hotels carry prices but only generic amenities, while the 24 google_places hotels carry richer amenities and no price at all. A price+amenity query is unsatisfiable by construction, not by ranking.

queries.question: the most affordable places to stay
budget friendly hotels near the city centre
cheapest rooms i can book tonight
economical hotels that are still well rated
cheap hotels that are still highly rated
save money on a colombo stay
low cost hotels with quick access to the centre
high end hotels with excellent ratings
